To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

weak gravitational lensing in the COSMOS field yields a lensing amplitude in agreement with the WMAP-5 best-fitting ACDM model, provides evidence for the accelerated expansion of our Universe, and demonstrates the feasibility of using space-based weak lensing to constrain the dark energy equation of state in future surveys.
weak gravitational lensing tomography of the COSMOS survey yields σ 8 (0.3/Ω m ) 0.51 ≡ 0.75±0.08, which is consistent with the WMAP-5 result.

the lensing signal in COSMOS is consistent with pure gravity, that it scales with redshift according to general relativity, and that it provides independent evidence for the accelerated expansion of our Universe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of weak lensing tomographic effects in the Cosmic Evolution Survey (cosmos) field.
the use of weak gravitational lensings as a probe of the dark energy.
the use of weak gravitational lens tomography as a tool to constrain cosmological parameters and the evolution of dark energy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are consistent with general relativity, the ACDM model, and a flat ΛCDM cosmology.
we have demonstrated that the lensing signal in COSMOS is fully consistent with a flat ACD cosmology and that we have provided independent evidence of the accelerating expansion of the Universe.

the lensing signal in COSMOS, combined with the WMAP data, is consistent with the predictions from the standard model of cosmology, and that the weak lens tomographic measurements provide independent evidence that the Universe is currently undergoing accelerated expansion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that weak lensing tomographic analysis is a promising method to study the dark energy and the expansion history of the Universe.

we have shown how weak gravitational lensing tomography is a very powerful tool for cosmological parameter estimation, and that the Hubble Space telescope COSMOS survey provides an ideal dataset for this analysis.
we have developed a weak lensing analysis that is optimized for space-based imaging data and applied it to the COSMOS data to measure the lensing amplitude.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lensing signal from the Hubble Space T elescope is robust, accurate, and consistent with the standard cosmological model.
weak lensing tomographic measurements are feasible from space-based data and that the lensing power spectrum can be measured with high precision.

, in the absence of significant systematic uncertainties and with a careful statistical analysis, weak lensing measurements of the redshift evolution of the cosmic shear can be used to constrain cosmological parameters, and in the future can be used to measure dark energy and the curvature of the Universe.
